sources: Unmodified original 300 x 300 Lichess Black-Knight.png and White-Knight.png; no high-resolution candidates used.
coordinates: Source PNG pixels; x right, y down, origin top left. All ellipse radii are source pixels.
method: Manually identify the front edge of the thin circular collar immediately below the horse. Back half is occluded.
At 2px x intervals, find strongest downward luminance derivative within +-3px of hand-picked anchors. Fit subpixel derivative peak quadratically.
Fit an axis-aligned ellipse by minimizing vertical pixel residual with Levenberg-Marquardt. Algebraic conic fit used only as initialization, not final estimate.
For a circular ring in a horizontal plane under orthographic or weak perspective, q=ry/rx=sin(camera elevation above horizontal). No camera elevation supplied to fitting.
Repeat with shorter arcs, shifted search windows and fixed-angle profile fits. Edge choice and partial-arc extrapolation dominate the uncertainty.
assumptions: Collar edge belongs to one horizontal circular ring.
Zero camera roll / ellipse axes aligned to image.
The same measured photometric edge follows the same geometric boundary around the visible arc.
limitations: A bright bevel or shadow can move the detected edge by a fraction of a pixel with azimuth; it is not an exact planar wire circle.
Only the front arc is observed. The centers and hidden back halves shown in annotations are inferred extrapolations.
Very small residuals do not imply accurate angle: different ellipses fit these short arcs within the original raster blur.
Black and white use the same geometry family and cannot be treated as fully independent statistical samples.
No fit used the outer fat-base silhouette as a planar circle. Exploratory base-groove fitting was rejected because the groove merges into curved shading and silhouette toward its ends.

summary.reliability: Low for absolute camera elevation; white ring is the stronger of the two. Useful only as a broad consistency check in a combined multi-piece fit.
summary.recommended_combination: Prefer the white collar profile at low weight; do not average the two point estimates as precise measurements. Fit sensitivity permits a broad range of elevated cameras. Use complete flatter rings from other pieces to determine the shared camera.

white.feature: Front lower edge of thin collar immediately under horse; back edge occluded.
white.sensitivity_interpretation: The half-pixel band is a practical raster-tolerance interval, NOT a probability confidence interval. Some alternative windows may select a neighboring bevel edge.
white.confidence: Low to moderate for a broad interval; low for a precise angle.

black.feature: Front lower edge of thin collar immediately under horse; back edge occluded.
black.sensitivity_interpretation: The half-pixel band is a practical raster-tolerance interval, NOT a probability confidence interval. Some alternative windows may select a neighboring bevel edge.

White.feature: lower base groove upper dark edge: exploratory, shadows ambiguous
White.status: REJECTED: no reliable single planar ring edge across chosen arc.
White.reason: White unconstrained geometric fit ran to q>1 (no valid horizontal circle elevation); black fit has >1.6px RMS and visually mixes groove, wood grain and curved-base shading.
